segments.speaker: Alan Clendenin
segments.text: Councilman Miranda.

segments.speaker: Charlie Miranda
segments.text: I'm not against that, but when you have strictly a debt, what you're asking for is a cost to the Taxpayers, then you have to include what the Taxpayers are getting for the amount of coffee, drinks, alcohol, whatever they buy and sell and how much percent do we get back -- equal equation.

segments.speaker: Lynn Hurtak
segments.text: I'm trying to find out where staff time is used.

segments.speaker: Charlie Miranda
segments.text: I understand. We don't know the other side.

segments.speaker: Bill Carlson
segments.text: Could we put that one as a separate one ahead of mine? Mine was really about whether we could ban the use or limit the use of stormwater money or enterprise money to be used on parades.

segments.speaker: Lynn Hurtak
segments.text: Agreed. To me this is tangential to have the money. Yes, I will make this a separate motion. Do I have to read it again?

segments.speaker: Alan Clendenin
segments.text: My concern is the date. I don't think it gives people -- that is a lot of information and that will require a lot of staff power.

segments.speaker: Lynn Hurtak
segments.text: He has the motion coming December 4. I have a feeling we'll end up with these questions of how is the -- like, how are we allocating --

segments.speaker: Alan Clendenin
segments.text: No Way they can get all that information.

segments.speaker: Lynn Hurtak
segments.text: They have to. They have to be able to monetize that.

segments.text: Now and then, stop everything and not do anything else between now and then?

segments.text: They should already have this information. It's part of auditing.

segments.text: Do they have the information?

segments.text: I'll ask Ms. Kopesky to work on it. How about this? I motion to have Ms. Kopesky work on summarizing the cost of events with the finance department. I will let you know at a future meeting whether or not it is successful or she can just e-mail it to everybody.

segments.speaker: Alan Clendenin
segments.text: We have a motion from Councilwoman Hurtak. Is there a second?

segments.speaker: Bill Carlson
segments.text: Second.

segments.speaker: Alan Clendenin
segments.text: Second from Councilman Carlson. Congratulations. This is what you're doing over Thanksgiving. We have a motion and second. All in favor, aye. Opposed? Ayes have it.

segments.text: That is it. Thank you.

segments.text: Okay. Mr. Maniscalco.

segments.text: Nothing. Thank you.

segments.text: Receive and file.

segments.text: Oh, Mr. Shelby, he has an announcement.

segments.text: I have an announcement, council. The purpose of this special called workshop is to discuss the framework for a resolution giving me direction to return to City Council with a draft that established the goals and objectives for the City Of Tampa Charter Review Advisory Commission and recommending amendments to the city charter. And guidelines for membership and the conduct of ITs meetings including a tentative timeline with the steps necessary for charter amendment language for voter consideration on the March 2nd, 2027 municipal election ballot. So, please, again, it is in the sister cities room down on the first floor. It is Monday. It begins at 1:00 in the afternoon.

segments.text: Thank you for the reminder. Ms. Kopesky, you wanted to say something? segments.speaker: Lynn Hurtak
segments.text: Yes. But generally we then look at the extra money and then try to decide what we want to do with it.

segments.speaker: Hagar Kopesky
segments.text: What would need to happen, there would need to be a new resolution as a '26 item.

segments.speaker: Lynn Hurtak
segments.text: Absolutely. We already talked about because we wouldn't be pulling it from this source. We would have to rewrite it anyway.

segments.speaker: Alan Clendenin
segments.text: That's if we do It That Way. Councilman Carlson.

segments.text: Just in preparation for the meeting, the charter meeting, in the instructions we got when on the Charter Review Commission, instead of recommending charter changes, there were a series of questions, like should we this or should we that. segments.speaker: Alan Clendenin
segments.text: Do not respond to the e-mail.

segments.speaker: Bill Carlson
segments.text: Don't respond to me. That Way you can think about them. Keep in mind, it's not a recommendation for a charter amendment. All we're doing is asking the question, how do we deal with this or should we. And then they will discuss it and decide if they want to come back to us with it.

segments.text: I'm sorry. If I understand correctly you will be sending out potential questions to be discussed at Monday's work session so they'll have advanced notice.

segments.text: Not questions to be answered on Monday. These are recommended questions that would go into the instructions. segments.speaker: Martin Shelby
segments.text: This Council at the workshop would have to tell me whether you want those questions in the resolution.

segments.text: If you don't like the questions, you can exit out and say we don't want it. That's what i'm going to propose.
